newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak foreign trade gap widens as imports surge.
newsitem.headline: Slovak foreign trade gap widens as imports surge.

text.p: Slovakia's foreign trade gap widened in July, spurred by a rise in car imports, fossile fuels and technology for the country's nuclear power programme, the Slovak Statistical Bureau said on Tuesday.

The Bureau (SUSR) said in a report the trade deficit for the first seven months of the year widened to 31.9 billion crowns, from 26.97 billion for January-June, with slow exports growth also a factor.
Imports grew 26.2 percent year-on-year to 182 billion crowns, while exports were up by four percent to 150 billion.
In 1995, the country had a seven-month trade surplus of 174 million crowns.

The SUSR said some 31 billion crowns of imports comprised fossil fuels and mineral oils. Imports for the construction of the Mochovce nuclear power plant took up 27.8 billion crowns, while car imports totalled 15.6 billion crowns.
"The imports volume was mainly influenced by higher imports of motor vehicles, airplanes and ships ... compared to the same period of last year," SUSR said.
"In decline were imports of computers and statistical software, chemicals, cane sugar, rapeseed and roasted coffee," it added.

The main export commodities were iron, rolled steel and metal semi-finished goods, accounting for 21.9 billion crowns in the seven month period, although the bureau said the volume of these exports were declining.
The Czech Republic remained Slovakia's biggest trading partner, accounting for 31.7 percent of total exports and 25.3 percent of imports.
Germany and Austria held on to second and third places as importers of Slovak goods, with a 20.4 and 5.9 percent share of the country's total exports.
The second and third largest share of Slovakia's imports come from the Russia and Germany, accounting for 18.6 and 14.4 percent, respectively.
Trade with OECD countries including former federation partner and western neighbour, the Czech Republic, was in deficit by 9.73 billion crowns, widening from 6.83 billion in the January-June period.
